esc-umbuntu-social-community-cultural-po.about:
ICYE Brazil invites volunteers to join the CAVAN Project, a Humanitarian Aid ESC initiative. This program offers a 6-month voluntary experience with the Umbúntu social project in a disadvantaged district of Alvorada city. Umbúntu provides a community and cultural space with workshops on topics like edible plant processing, handicrafts, capoeira, percussion, and language teaching. Volunteers will have a hands-on experience in environmentally sustainable practices by participating in farming, permaculture gardening, construction and other manual activities of our project. The main aims are to provide humanitarian aid, raise awareness about climate change and encourage discussions on green alternatives. Join us now!

Umbúntu’s focus on organic produce allows volunteers to enjoy and prepare healthy food. As in every ESC placement, volunteers receive insurance, pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate. Humanitarian aid placements also include specific pre-deployment training and security briefings.

esc-unpolished-unfiltered-kaunas-2027.about:
Kaunas Artists’ House is not just a cultural institution — it is a shifting stage, a testing ground, a beautifully imperfect organism at the heart of Kaunas. A place where ideas are tried before they are safe, where art is allowed to be messy, political, tender, loud — and deeply human. A platform for bold ideas, disobedient creativity, and encounters that don’t always fit neatly into categories. This is where performance spills beyond the stage. Where identities are explored, questioned, rehearsed. Where communities don’t just gather — they transform each other. Through contemporary art, residencies and community-driven events, we create encounters that are sometimes unexpected, sometimes uncomfortable — but always meaningful. Tasks: Co-create and run creative workshops Bring events to life — set up, shape atmosphere, welcome guests Connect with Kaunas’ international community Collaborate on cultural events Develop and implement your own creative project

Schools from ~14 countries
International Final for top senior teams
ethics-olympiad-2026-27.eligibility: School teams: Middle School ages 11–14 (Years 7–9); Senior School ages 15–18 (Years 10–13); open to schools internationally.

Form a team and study the published cases
Compete in the online heats
Qualify for the International Final

eurobot-2027.about:
Created in 1998, Eurobot challenges teams to design and build autonomous robots that complete a set of tasks on a themed table within 100 seconds; the 2027 season's rules were published in October 2026. Teams first compete in their national cup run by a National Organising Committee; the best qualify for the international finals.

The event is held in Europe but welcomes teams from all continents. Countries without a national committee can contact Eurobot about direct participation.
highlights: Autonomous robots, new theme each year
National cups then international finals (5–8 May 2027)
Junior version for school teams
eurobot-2027.eligibility: Student and youth teams (university clubs, schools, maker clubs) through their country's Eurobot National Organising Committee; Eurobot Junior for younger students.

Contact your National Organising Committee to register
Build and test your robot over the season
Compete at the national cup to qualify for the finals
eurobot-2027.costs: Team registration fees set by national committees; robot materials and travel are self-funded.

european-commission-blue-book-traineeshi.about:
The Blue Book Traineeship Programme places graduates for five paid months in the European Commission, its executive and decentralised agencies, Commissioners' cabinets and the European External Action Service. Trainees get hands-on experience of EU policy-making and administration in a multicultural team.

The programme is open to university graduates of all nationalities, so students from Georgia can apply alongside EU citizens; there are dedicated IT traineeships and a newer strand for graduates of vocational education and training (VET). Selection is competitive: candidates are pre-selected and then recruited by Commission services.

Registration for the October 2027 session opens on 15 February 2027 and closes on 12 March 2027 (10:00 Brussels time). Apply early and make sure your language certificates and degree documents are ready.
highlights: Paid five-month traineeship in EU institutions
Open to graduates of any nationality, including Georgia
IT and vocational (VET) strands available
european-commission-blue-book-traineeshi.eligibility: University graduates (or VET graduates for the VET strand) of any nationality; very good knowledge of English, French or German plus another EU language for EU nationals; no previous traineeship or employment in an EU institution over six weeks. Check the full rules on the programme site.
how_to_apply: Create an EU Login account and read the Blue Book rules
Prepare your degree, transcripts and language evidence
Register online between 15 Feb and 12 Mar 2027 (10:00 Brussels time)
If pre-selected, you may be contacted by Commission services for interviews
european-commission-blue-book-traineeshi.costs: Paid: trainees receive a monthly grant; travel costs are reimbursed under the programme rules.

european-parliament-mep-office-traineesh.about:
Besides the Schuman traineeships in Parliament's Secretariat, individual Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) may offer paid traineeships in their own offices in Brussels (or Strasbourg), based on an agreement with the Parliament. Trainees support the MEP's legislative and political work and see day-to-day parliamentary life up close.

MEPs choose their trainees freely, but candidates must be 18+ (derogations possible), nationals of an EU Member State or an accession/candidate country (Georgia qualifies; MEPs may also take third-country nationals who meet visa rules), have completed secondary school plus higher, technical or vocational study (or hold a university diploma), know one official EU language well, and not have done a previous traineeship with an MEP or worked as an MEP assistant.

There is no central call: identify MEPs whose committees and political priorities match your interests and approach their offices directly.
highlights: Paid, hands-on experience with an elected MEP
Open to nationals of EU candidate countries, including Georgia
No fixed window: apply directly any time of year
european-parliament-mep-office-traineesh.eligibility: 18+; EU or accession/candidate-country nationality (Georgia qualifies); secondary school plus higher/technical/vocational study or a university diploma; thorough knowledge of one official EU language; no prior MEP traineeship or work as an MEP assistant; no other employment contract during the traineeship.
how_to_apply: Read the MEP traineeship rules on the European Parliament traineeships page
Shortlist MEPs whose work matches your field
Email the MEP's office a CV and tailored motivation letter
If accepted, the MEP's office completes the traineeship agreement with Parliament
european-parliament-mep-office-traineesh.costs: Paid traineeship (allowance set under the European Parliament rules for MEP trainees).

european-parliament-schuman-traineeship-.about:
Schuman traineeships are paid five-month placements in the Secretariat of the European Parliament, in Brussels, Luxembourg, Strasbourg or a Liaison Office. Trainees work in fields such as EU internal and external policy, finance, law, translation and multilingualism, communication, administration and IT, and see from inside how EU laws are made.

Applicants must be 18+, hold a full university degree (or, for a few places, a vocational qualification obtained in the EU), and be nationals of an EU Member State or an accession/candidate country, which includes Georgia. Non-EU citizens need very good English, French or German. You may apply for up to three traineeships.

There are two intakes a year: for 1 October – end of February you apply 1–31 May; for 1 March – 31 July you apply 1–31 October. A monthly grant is paid, and trainees with disabilities can receive extra support through a Positive Action Scheme.
highlights: Paid traineeship inside an EU institution
Open to nationals of EU candidate countries, including Georgia
Wide range of departments: policy, law, communication, IT
european-parliament-schuman-traineeship-.eligibility: Aged 18+; EU or accession/candidate-country nationality (Georgia qualifies; a few places for other nationalities); full university degree (EQF 6) or, for limited places, an EU vocational qualification; very good English, French or German for non-EU nationals; no more than two months previous work/traineeship in an EU body.
how_to_apply: Read the Schuman traineeship rules and FAQ on the European Parliament page
Create an account on the EP traineeship application platform
Select up to three traineeship offers and submit between 1 and 31 May 2027
If shortlisted, upload supporting documents (degree, language, criminal record)
european-parliament-schuman-traineeship-.costs: Paid: monthly grant plus allowances (see the EP "Monthly grant and allowances" document). Travel and living costs are covered by the grant.

european-prize-women-innovators-rising-i.about:
The European Prize for Women Innovators is jointly awarded by the European Innovation Council and the European Institute of Innovation and Technology. It celebrates women who founded or co-founded innovative companies and turned ideas into real products and services.

In 2027 there are three categories: Women Innovators (€100,000 / €70,000 / €50,000), Rising Innovators for women under 35 (€50,000 / €30,000 / €20,000) and EIT Women Leadership. Applicants must legally reside in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe associated country, which explicitly includes Georgia, Armenia, Moldova and Ukraine, and their company must be established there.

Beyond the money, finalists get Europe-wide visibility and an award ceremony in the second quarter of 2027. Young founders should look at the Rising Innovators category.
highlights: Rising Innovators: up to €50,000 for women under 35
Explicitly open to founders in Georgia
Europe-wide visibility for finalists
european-prize-women-innovators-rising-i.eligibility: Women applying as natural persons, legally resident in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe associated country (incl. Georgia); founder or co-founder of an innovative company established in one of those countries. Rising Innovators: under 35. See the Rules of the Contest.
how_to_apply: Read the Rules of the Contest on the EIT/EIC page
Choose your category (Rising Innovators if under 35)
Apply through the EU Funding & Tenders portal before 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 CET
european-prize-women-innovators-rising-i.costs: Free to apply. Prizes from €20,000 to €100,000.

european-space-camp-2027.about:
European Space Camp (ESC) is an annual, non-profit week-long camp at the Andøya Space rocket range in northern Norway, run by former participants. Campers attend lectures on space science and rocket physics, work in groups on a hands-on rocket campaign (building payloads, analysing data) and launch a real student rocket, while meeting science-minded peers from around the world.

You cannot pay to attend: every place is tied to a scholarship (from ESA for nationals of ESA member states, national sponsors, and an 'International' seat open to any country). Scholarships cover all costs at camp; some do not cover travel. Applications have two rounds; round one asks for a video, CV and proof of English.
highlights: Launch a real rocket at the Andøya Space range
All seats are scholarships covering camp costs
International seat open to applicants from any country
european-space-camp-2027.eligibility: Young people aged 17–20 (2027 birth-year window to be published), with a documented passion for science and fluent English. Any nationality; specific scholarships have nationality rules.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on spacecamp.no
When the 2027 window opens, upload a video, CV and proof of English proficiency (round 1)
Check which scholarship seats you are eligible for (international or national)
Complete round 2 if shortlisted
european-space-camp-2027.costs: Free for selected campers: scholarships cover all camp costs; some scholarships do not cover travel to Norway.

experiment-ev-jubilee-scholarship-2027-2.about:
Experiment e.V., Germany's oldest non-profit exchange organisation (95 years), awards a Jubilee Scholarship of up to 9,500 euros for a full school year abroad in any of its programme countries, departing summer 2027. Selection is based on financial situation and motivation: applicants submit a creative contribution (video, podcast, photo collage or similar) on how they would foster intercultural dialogue between the host country and Germany.

Apply online for an Experiment school year, then email the scholarship application and motivation letter to kortenbusch@experiment-ev.de by 30 November. Experiment also offers partial scholarships (up to 3,000 euros), Europe, climate and social-media scholarships with a 31 January deadline.

Creative application format
Deadline 30 November 2026

Create your intercultural-dialogue contribution (video, podcast, collage...)
Email application and motivation letter to kortenbusch@experiment-ev.de by 30 Nov 2026
experiment-ev-jubilee-scholarship-2027-2.costs: Up to 9,500 euros towards the programme fee; Auslands-BAföG can be combined.

experiment-ev-partial-scholarships-summe.about:
Experiment e.V. funds school exchanges for summer 2027 departures with several scholarships, all due 31 January 2027: income-based partial scholarships up to 3,000 euros (all countries and lengths; apply for Auslands-BAföG in parallel); the Europa scholarship up to 1,000 euros for a semester or year in Europe (motivation letter with an idea for intercultural understanding); the Klima scholarship up to 500 euros for travelling to Belgium, Italy, Spain or France by train or ferry; and the Social-Media scholarship up to 1,000 euros (3-minute video in German, not income-based).

Partner funds include the Kreuzberger Kinderstiftung (up to 80% for non-Gymnasium students, mainly eastern Germany and Berlin, Europe only) and RuhrTalente. If you do not receive a scholarship you may withdraw free of charge within a set period.

Income-based and creative options
Deadline 31 January 2027

Submit by 31 Jan 2027 (summer departure)

expo-2027-belgrade-playmakers-volunteers.about:
Expo 2027 Belgrade is a specialised World Expo recognised by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE), running for 93 days in 2027 under the theme "Play for Humanity: Sport and Music for All". Its volunteer programme, Expo Playmakers, is the largest in Serbia's history, with 48 roles including visitor and delegation services, logistics, event operations and support for international teams.

The programme is open to adults from Serbia and abroad (applicants must be 18 by 15 April 2027) who can serve at least 15 days during the Expo. More than 10,000 people from 119 countries had applied by August 2026. Selected volunteers receive general and specialised training, including multicultural communication.

Benefits include an official uniform and welcome pack, a certificate endorsed by the BIE, extra ECTS credits for students, Air Serbia flight discounts of up to 27%, and free rides on selected Srbijavoz trains in Serbia. Accommodation is not mentioned, so international volunteers should plan their own stay.
highlights: World Expo volunteering in Belgrade, open to international applicants
Minimum 15 days; 48 different roles
BIE-endorsed certificate, ECTS credits and Air Serbia flight discounts
expo-2027-belgrade-playmakers-volunteers.eligibility: Adults of any nationality who are 18 by 15 April 2027 and available for at least 15 days during the Expo. Check Serbia's visa rules for your passport before applying.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the official volunteer portal (join.volunteer.expobelgrade2027.org).
Fill in the application with your availability, languages and preferred roles.
Complete the selection steps and the general and specialised training (mainly autumn 2026 – spring 2027).
Questions: playmakers@expobelgrade2027.org.
expo-2027-belgrade-playmakers-volunteers.costs: Free. Uniform, welcome package, training and certificate provided; up to 27% off Air Serbia flights and free selected Srbijavoz trains. Accommodation and meals are not stated as covered.

fao-world-food-day-poster-contest-2026.about:
Every year FAO invites children and teenagers to create a poster on the World Food Day theme, raising awareness of hunger, nutrition and sustainable food systems. There are four age categories: 5–8, 9–12, 13–15 and 16–19.

Entries are submitted as a digital JPEG through the online form (one entry per person; generative AI images are not allowed, though AI-assisted ideation or editing must be disclosed). Fifteen posters per category are shortlisted in December 2026, and three winners per category are showcased on FAO's World Food Day website and social media, with certificates and gift bags.
highlights: Run by a UN agency
Free, open worldwide, ages 5–19
Winners promoted by FAO globally
fao-world-food-day-poster-contest-2026.eligibility: Anyone aged 5–19 anywhere in the world (minors need parental permission); one entry per person; FAO staff families excluded.
how_to_apply: Read the World Food Day 2026 theme and rules
Create your poster (drawing, painting, digital art) — up to 25 words of text
Photograph or scan it as a JPEG
Submit via the online form before 6 Nov 2026, 12:00 CET

faspe-fellowships-2027.about:
FASPE (Fellowships at Auschwitz for the Study of Professional Ethics) brings small cohorts of graduate students and early-career professionals to Berlin, Kraków and the Auschwitz memorial site. By studying how doctors, lawyers, business leaders, journalists, engineers and clergy contributed to the crimes of Nazi Germany, fellows examine the ethical choices they will face in their own professions today.

There are six programmes: Law, Business and Design & Technology run 28 May – 11 June 2027; Medical, Clergy & Religious Leaders and Journalism run 18 June – 2 July 2027. Seminars are led by expert faculty, and fellows join a lifelong alumni network and later workshops.

The fellowship is fully funded: FASPE covers round-trip airfare (also for fellows travelling from outside the United States), hotels, group meals, admission fees, local transport and pocket money. Applications close on 3 January 2027 via Submittable.
highlights: Fully funded, including international airfare
Six tracks: law, business, medicine, journalism, design/tech, clergy
Study visits in Berlin, Kraków and Auschwitz
faspe-fellowships-2027.eligibility: Graduate students and early-career professionals in law, business, medicine, journalism, design/technology or religious leadership. International applicants can apply (FASPE covers travel to Berlin from outside the US).

Prepare essays and a CV.
Arrange recommendation letters (faculty or supervisor), due 10 January 2027.
Submit the application on Submittable by 3 January 2027.
faspe-fellowships-2027.costs: Fully funded: airfare, hotels, group meals, admissions, materials, local travel and pocket money.

fifa-womens-world-cup-brazil-2027-volunt.about:
The FIFA Women's World Cup Brazil 2027 will be played in Belo Horizonte, Brasília, Fortaleza, Porto Alegre, Recife, Rio de Janeiro, Salvador and São Paulo. FIFA opened volunteer applications on 3 September 2026 and plans to recruit more than 6,000 volunteers; over 100,000 people had registered interest, and shortlisted applicants are invited to interviews on a rolling basis.

Volunteers must be 18 or over, Brazilian or legally permitted to enter Brazil for the tournament, available for seven to ten shifts in June–July 2027, and speak Portuguese or English (other languages are a plus). No previous volunteering experience is required. Selected volunteers receive training and support from experienced staff.

Benefits include meals during shifts, a full adidas uniform, transport within the host city and recognition gifts. Note that only the application on volunteer.fifa.com counts; earlier "register your interest" sign-ups are not applications.
highlights: First Women's World Cup in South America, eight host cities
No experience needed; Portuguese or English required
Meals, adidas uniform and local transport provided

Select the FIFA Women's World Cup Brazil 2027 and complete the application form.
Complete the short online assessment.
If shortlisted, attend the interview and training.
fifa-womens-world-cup-brazil-2027-volunt.costs: Free. Meals on shift, adidas uniform and transport within the host city provided. International travel and accommodation are not covered.

fintech-innovation-lab-new-york-2027.about:
Launched in 2010 by the Partnership Fund for New York City and Accenture, the FinTech Innovation Lab New York is a 12-week mentorship programme that pairs fintech and insurtech companies with senior executives from dozens of major banks, insurers and financial institutions. TIME listed it among America's Best Incubators & Accelerators 2026.

It is for early- to growth-stage technology companies (often with an enterprise-ready product) that want to refine and pilot their solution with large financial institutions; companies from outside the US have taken part. The Lab takes no equity and charges no fee.

Applications for the 2027 class opened on 5 October 2026 on the Lab's New York apply page.
highlights: No equity, no fee
Mentorship from senior executives at major financial firms
Strong pilot and customer opportunities
fintech-innovation-lab-new-york-2027.eligibility: Early- to growth-stage fintech and insurtech companies from any country able to take part in New York sessions.
how_to_apply: Read the New York programme page.
Prepare company details, product and traction.
Submit the online application for the 2027 class.
Interview with the Lab and partner institutions if shortlisted.
fintech-innovation-lab-new-york-2027.costs: Free; no equity taken. Travel to New York is at the company's own cost.

flex-global-argentina-2027-28.about:
FLEX Global is the U.S. Department of State's merit-based high-school exchange that merges the Future Leaders Exchange (FLEX, 30+ years) and the Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES, almost 25 years). It is implemented by American Councils for International Education with AFS, Amideast and iEARN. Argentina is one of 31 countries in the 2027-28 cycle. Finalists live with a screened volunteer host family, attend a U.S. high school for the full year, do community service and take part in 'American Excellence' activities on business, technology and entrepreneurship.

Selection is free and runs in rounds: English testing, proctored essays, interviews with FLEX Global staff and a full application; final selection is made in the U.S., and English is only one factor. Finalists pass a medical check, learn their status in spring 2027, attend a pre-departure orientation at home in June or July, fly to the U.S. in August 2027 and return in May-June 2028. Placement anywhere in the U.S. is assigned, mostly in small towns and suburbs.

In Argentina the programme is run by the national office (https://afs.org.ar/flexglobal, flexglobal.arg@afs.org). AFS Argentina page: 'Postulaciones abiertas del 7 de octubre al 1 de noviembre de 2026'. ELTiS English test (B1) is part of preselection.

Good academic standing, previous English study, U.S. J-1 visa eligibility and an international passport. Not eligible: students whose family has applied or plans to emigrate to the U.S.; usually not those who will have graduated before departure.
how_to_apply: Check eligibility in the 2027-28 FLEX Global brochure (Argentina: last 3 years of secondary school, born 15 Jan 2010 - 15 Aug 2012)
Apply online / contact the Argentina office (flexglobal.arg@afs.org) before the deadline
Take the English test and write the proctored essays
